claim: Malaria transmission relies on the production of gametes following ingestion by a mosquito.
source: Malaria transmission relies on the production of gametes following ingestion by a mosquito.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about malaria transmission.

claim: Ca2+-dependent protein kinase 4 controls three processes essential to progress from a single haploid microgametocyte to the release of eight flagellated microgametes in Plasmodium berghei.
source: Here, we show that Ca2+-dependent protein kinase 4 controls three processes essential to progress from a single haploid microgametocyte to the release of eight flagellated microgametes in Plasmodium berghei.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: A myristoylated isoform of CDPK4 is activated by Ca2+ to initiate a first genome replication within twenty seconds of activation.
source: A myristoylated isoform is activated by Ca2+ to initiate a first genome replication within twenty seconds of activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the timing and requirement of CDPK4 activity.

claim: The role of CDPK4 in initiating genome replication is mediated by a protein of the SAPS-domain family involved in S-phase entry.
source: This role is mediated by a protein of the SAPS-domain family involved in S-phase entry.
evidence: This is supported by the identification and characterization of SOC1 in the study.

claim: CDPK4 is required for the assembly of the mitotic spindle.
source: At the same time, CDPK4 is required for the assembly of the subsequent mitotic spindle and to phosphorylate a microtubule-associated protein important for mitotic spindle formation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing defects in mitotic spindle formation when CDPK4 is inhibited.

claim: CDPK4 phosphorylates a microtubule-associated protein important for mitotic spindle formation.
source: At the same time, CDPK4 is required for the assembly of the subsequent mitotic spindle and to phosphorylate a microtubule-associated protein important for mitotic spindle formation.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomics data identifying SOC2 as a substrate.

claim: A non-myristoylated isoform of CDPK4 is essential to complete cytokinesis by activating motility of the male flagellum.
source: Finally, a non-myristoylated isoform is essential to complete cytokinesis by activating motility of the male flagellum.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with CDPK4M57A mutants and characterization of SOC3.

claim: The late role of CDPK4 in completing cytokinesis has been linked to phosphorylation of an uncharacterised flagellar protein.
source: This role has been linked to phosphorylation of an uncharacterised flagellar protein.
evidence: This is supported by the identification of SOC3 as a CDPK4 substrate localized to axonemes.

claim: Malaria is caused by vector-borne protozoan parasites of the genus Plasmodium that cycle between mosquitoes and vertebrate hosts.
source: Malaria is caused by vector-borne protozoan parasites of the genus Plasmodium that cycle between mosquitoes and vertebrate hosts.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about malaria.

claim: Malaria pathology is linked to the proliferation of asexual blood stage parasites.
source: Malaria pathology is linked to the proliferation of asexual blood stage parasites, whereas transmission to the mosquito is mediated by an obligatory sexual life cycle phase.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about malaria pathology.

claim: Transmission to the mosquito is mediated by an obligatory sexual life cycle phase.
source: Malaria pathology is linked to the proliferation of asexual blood stage parasites, whereas transmission to the mosquito is mediated by an obligatory sexual life cycle phase.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about malaria transmission.

claim: Differentiation from asexually replicating stages into non-dividing male and female gametocytes takes place inside red blood cells.
source: Differentiation from asexually replicating stages into non-dividing male and female gametocytes takes place inside red blood cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Plasmodium development.

claim: Gametocytes resume their development by responding to environmental signals including xanthurenic acid (XA) and a simultaneous drop in temperature.
source: Gametocytes resume their development by responding to environmental signals including a small mosquito molecule, xanthurenic acid (XA), and a simultaneous drop in temperature (Billker et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Within 10 min of mosquito ingestion, Plasmodium male gametocyte completes three rounds of genome replication followed by endomitosis within a single nucleus.
source: Within 10 min, it completes three rounds of genome replication followed by endomitosis within a single nucleus, assembles the component parts of eight axonemes, and escapes the red blood cell in a process called exflagellation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about male gametocyte development.

claim: Male gametocytes assemble the component parts of eight axonemes within 10 minutes of mosquito ingestion.
source: Within 10 min, it completes three rounds of genome replication followed by endomitosis within a single nucleus, assembles the component parts of eight axonemes, and escapes the red blood cell in a process called exflagellation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about male gametocyte development.

claim: Male gametocytes escape the red blood cell in a process called exflagellation.
source: Within 10 min, it completes three rounds of genome replication followed by endomitosis within a single nucleus, assembles the component parts of eight axonemes, and escapes the red blood cell in a process called exflagellation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about male gametocyte development.

claim: Circulating microgametocytes are arrested at a G0-like stage of the cell cycle at the haploid level.
source: Circulating microgametocytes are arrested at a G0-like stage of the cell cycle at the haploid level.
evidence: This is established knowledge about microgametocyte cell cycle state.

claim: After 15 s of induction by XA, eight basal bodies are assembled from a single microtubule organising centre.
source: After 15 s of induction by XA, eight basal bodies are assembled from a single microtubule organising centre (Sinden et al., 1976).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: After 1 min of XA induction, the first genome replication is completed and the spindle of mitosis I is formed.
source: After 1 min, the first genome replication is completed and the spindle of mitosis I is formed (Billker et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Each basal body nucleates one of the eight axonemes from large quantities of tubulin contained in the cytoplasm.
source: At the same time each basal body nucleates one of the eight axonemes from large quantities of tubulin contained in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is established knowledge about axoneme assembly.

claim: By six minutes after XA induction, the four spindles of mitosis III have formed.
source: By six minutes, the four spindles of mitosis III have formed and chromatin condensation only sets in at the end of mitosis III.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the timing of mitosis during gametogenesis.

claim: Chromatin condensation only sets in at the end of mitosis III.
source: By six minutes, the four spindles of mitosis III have formed and chromatin condensation only sets in at the end of mitosis III.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromatin condensation timing.

claim: Gametocytes escape their host cell following the exocytosis of specialised secretory vesicles containing proteins with membranolytic activities.
source: In parallel gametocytes escape their host cell following the exocytosis of specialised secretory vesicles containing proteins with membranolytic activities.
evidence: This is established knowledge about gametocyte egress.

claim: At the onset of exflagellation, axonemes become motile and swim out of the residual gametocyte body.
source: At the onset of exflagellation, axonemes become motile and swim out of the residual gametocyte body.
evidence: This is established knowledge about exflagellation.

claim: Each basal body remains attached to a mitotic spindle pole and drags a haploid genome that is incorporated into the exflagellating gamete.
source: As each basal body remains attached to a mitotic spindle pole, they drag a haploid genome that is incorporated into the exflagellating gamete.
evidence: This is established knowledge about genome incorporation during exflagellation.

claim: Malaria parasites are highly divergent from model organisms.
source: Malaria parasites are highly divergent from model organisms and significant differences in the composition and properties of cell cycle regulators have been reported (Gerald et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Significant differences in the composition and properties of cell cycle regulators have been reported in malaria parasites.
source: Malaria parasites are highly divergent from model organisms and significant differences in the composition and properties of cell cycle regulators have been reported (Gerald et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Gametocyte stimulation by XA is followed by Ca2+ mobilisation from internal stores after a lag phase of ~10 s.
source: Gametocyte stimulation by XA is followed by Ca2+ mobilisation from internal stores after a lag phase of ~10 s (Billker et al., 2004) which requires active cGMP-dependent protein kinase G, PKG (Brochet and Billker, 2016; Brochet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ca2+ mobilisation requires active cGMP-dependent protein kinase G, PKG.
source: Gametocyte stimulation by XA is followed by Ca2+ mobilisation from internal stores after a lag phase of ~10 s (Billker et al., 2004) which requires active cGMP-dependent protein kinase G, PKG (Brochet and Billker, 2016; Brochet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In activated microgametocytes, CDPK4 is required to enter S-phase in Plasmodium berghei.
source: In activated microgametocytes, the plant-like Ca2+-dependent protein kinase 4 (CDPK4), which belongs to a family absent from the human genome, is required to enter S-phase in the rodent parasite Plasmodium berghei (Billker et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4 belongs to a family absent from the human genome.
source: In activated microgametocytes, the plant-like Ca2+-dependent protein kinase 4 (CDPK4), which belongs to a family absent from the human genome, is required to enter S-phase in the rodent parasite Plasmodium berghei (Billker et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CDPK4.

claim: Selective inhibitors of CDPK4 block exflagellation of P. berghei in vivo.
source: Selective inhibitors of CDPK4 were shown to block exflagellation of P. berghei in vivo and of the human parasite P. falciparum in vitro placing CDPK4 as a promising drug target to reduce transmission of malaria (Ojo et al., 2014, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Selective inhibitors of CDPK4 block exflagellation of P. falciparum in vitro.
source: Selective inhibitors of CDPK4 were shown to block exflagellation of P. berghei in vivo and of the human parasite P. falciparum in vitro placing CDPK4 as a promising drug target to reduce transmission of malaria (Ojo et al., 2014, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CDPK4 is a promising drug target to reduce transmission of malaria.
source: Selective inhibitors of CDPK4 were shown to block exflagellation of P. berghei in vivo and of the human parasite P. falciparum in vitro placing CDPK4 as a promising drug target to reduce transmission of malaria (Ojo et al., 2014, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference based on cited experimental results.

claim: The molecular functions of CDPK4 remain unknown.
source: Despite the importance of CDPK4 for transmission to the mosquito vector, its molecular functions remain unknown and none of its substrates have been identified.
evidence: This statement describes the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: None of CDPK4's substrates have been identified prior to this study.
source: Despite the importance of CDPK4 for transmission to the mosquito vector, its molecular functions remain unknown and none of its substrates have been identified.
evidence: This statement describes the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: CDPK4 plays at least three distinct roles during male gametogenesis.
source: By combining reverse and chemical genetics with molecular and cellular phenotyping, we found that CDPK4 plays at least three distinct roles during male gametogenesis and we identified three effectors mediating each of these roles.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Three effectors mediating each of CDPK4's roles have been identified.
source: By combining reverse and chemical genetics with molecular and cellular phenotyping, we found that CDPK4 plays at least three distinct roles during male gametogenesis and we identified three effectors mediating each of these roles.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Compound 1294 was found to inhibit P. falciparum exflagellation through CDPK4.
source: One of these, compound 1294, was found to inhibit P. falciparum exflagellation through CDPK4 (Ojo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4S147M-3xHA parasites show a fitness cost preventing exflagellation.
source: We however discovered that introduction of both a C-terminal 3xHA epitope tag and a S147M substitution imposed a fitness cost on CDPK4 function preventing exflagellation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exflagellation is delayed in CDPK4-3xHA parasites.
source: Investigation of the effect of each single modification revealed exflagellation is delayed in CDPK4-3xHA but not in CDPK4S147M parasites.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exflagellation is not delayed in CDPK4S147M parasites.
source: Investigation of the effect of each single modification revealed exflagellation is delayed in CDPK4-3xHA but not in CDPK4S147M parasites.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: S147M substitution only imposes a minor cost that does not impact on exflagellation on its own.
source: This indicates that a S147M substitution only imposes a minor cost that, on its own, does not impact on exflagellation.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data comparing different mutants.

claim: CDPK4S147M transgenic parasites showed a ~ 50 fold decrease in exflagellation susceptibility to 1294 compared to the parental wild-type strain.
source: Compared to the parental wild-type strain, CDPK4S147M transgenic parasites showed a ~ 50 fold decrease in exflagellation susceptibility to 1294.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: 1 µM 1294 blocked exflagellation by specifically targeting CDPK4.
source: Importantly, 1 µM 1294 blocked exflagellation by specifically targeting CDPK4 and this concentration was further used this study (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating specificity through the resistant mutant.

claim: CDPK4 activity is required between 10 and 20 s to initiate the first round of DNA replication.
source: CDPK4 activity is required between 10 and 20 s to initiate the first round of DNA replication and the second genome replication.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CDPK4 activity is not required for DNA replication per se.
source: CDPK4 activity is however not required for DNA replication per se.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that DNA replication proceeds normally when 1294 is added after 20 seconds.

claim: Addition of 1294 prior to activation dramatically reduced the ability of male gametocytes to replicate their genome.
source: Addition of 1294 prior to activation dramatically reduced the ability of male gametocytes to replicate their genome as previously described for CDPK4-KO parasites (Billker et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and citation to previous work.

claim: 25% of microgametocytes progress to the diploid state when 1294 is added prior to activation.
source: We were however able to detect 25% of microgametocytes progressing to the diploid state but not further to the tetra- or octoploid levels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: When 1294 was added 20 s after activation, no inhibition of DNA replication was observed.
source: When 1294 was added 20 s after activation, no inhibition of DNA replication was observed.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CDPK4 activity between 0 and 20 s post-activation is important for the 1N/2N and subsequent 2N/4N transitions.
source: Altogether, this reveals that CDPK4 activity between 0 and 20 s post-activation is important for the 1N/2N and subsequent 2N/4N transitions but not for DNA replication per se.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data showing timing of CDPK4 requirement.

claim: Almost no diploid parasites reached the tetraploid state when CDPK4 is inhibited.
source: Interestingly, almost no diploid parasites reached the tetraploid state suggesting that CDPK4 plays a second role between the first and second rounds of genome replication.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CDPK4 plays a second role between the first and second rounds of genome replication.
source: Interestingly, almost no diploid parasites reached the tetraploid state suggesting that CDPK4 plays a second role between the first and second rounds of genome replication.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data.

claim: In DMSO treated parasites, 64% of male gametocytes showed spindle-like structures 1 min after activation.
source: In DMSO treated parasites, 64% of male gametocytes showed spindle-like structures while this proportion decreased to 7% in parasites treated with 1294 (Figure 1D) indicating that CDPK4 activity is also required for mitotic spindle formation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: In 1294 treated parasites, 7% of male gametocytes showed spindle-like structures 1 min after activation.
source: In DMSO treated parasites, 64% of male gametocytes showed spindle-like structures while this proportion decreased to 7% in parasites treated with 1294 (Figure 1D) indicating that CDPK4 activity is also required for mitotic spindle formation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: CDPK4 activity is required for mitotic spindle formation.
source: In DMSO treated parasites, 64% of male gametocytes showed spindle-like structures while this proportion decreased to 7% in parasites treated with 1294 (Figure 1D) indicating that CDPK4 activity is also required for mitotic spindle formation.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data showing reduced spindle formation when CDPK4 is inhibited.

claim: When 1294 is added 30 s after activation, parasites normally develop to the 8N state and assemble axonemes.
source: To do so, we added 1294 30 s after activation, a time point at which CDPK4 is not required to initiate DNA replication anymore. With such a treatment, parasites normally developed to the 8N state and assembled axonemes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1E.

claim: When 1294 is added 30 s after activation, DNA does not condense, axonemes remain around the nucleus and no exflagellation is observed.
source: However, DNA did not condense, axonemes remained around the nucleus and no exflagellation was observed (Figure 1C and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1E.

claim: A similar phenotype is observed when 1294 is added at 9 min post-activation.
source: A similar phenotype was observed when 1294 was added only seconds prior to the initial exflagellation events at 9 min post-activation (Figure 1C and E–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, 1E, and 1F.

claim: When added at 15 min post-activation, 1294 does not inhibit flagellar beating.
source: However, when added at 15 min post-activation, 1294 did not inhibit flagellar beating (Figure 1G) or ookinete formation and motility (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 parts 9 and 10).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: When added at 15 min post-activation, 1294 does not inhibit ookinete formation and motility.
source: However, when added at 15 min post-activation, 1294 did not inhibit flagellar beating (Figure 1G) or ookinete formation and motility (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 parts 9 and 10).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 parts 9 and 10.

claim: CDPK4 activity is redundant between 30 s and 9 min after activation.
source: Altogether, this shows that CDPK4 activity seems to be redundant between 30 s and 9 min after activation but is further required at a late stage immediately preceding the onset of axoneme motility, DNA condensation and cytokinesis.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data showing no effect of 1294 addition during this time window.

claim: CDPK4 is required at a late stage immediately preceding the onset of axoneme motility, DNA condensation and cytokinesis.
source: Altogether, this shows that CDPK4 activity seems to be redundant between 30 s and 9 min after activation but is further required at a late stage immediately preceding the onset of axoneme motility, DNA condensation and cytokinesis.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data showing effects of 1294 addition at 9 min.

claim: A total of 150 proteins were immunoprecipitated in both CDPK4-3xHA and CDPK4-2xmyc lysates after cross-linking but not in a WT control.
source: A total of 150 proteins were immunoprecipitated in both CDPK4-3xHA and CDPK4-2xmyc lysates after cross-linking but not in a WT control (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 parts 1 to 3 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: MCM2-7/Cdt1 and ORC proteins are the most enriched molecular components in CDPK4 immunoprecipitates.
source: MCM2-7/Cdt1 and ORC proteins that are part of the pre-replicative complex represented the most enriched molecular components (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by GO term enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Proteins of the microtubule cytoskeleton were enriched in CDPK4 immunoprecipitates.
source: Proteins of the microtubule cytoskeleton and of the replisome were also enriched including polymerases α, δ, and ε, the proliferating nuclear antigen, replication factor C complexes and replication factor A.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Proteins of the replisome were enriched in CDPK4 immunoprecipitates, including polymerases α, δ, and ε, the proliferating nuclear antigen, replication factor C complexes and replication factor A.
source: Proteins of the microtubule cytoskeleton and of the replisome were also enriched including polymerases α, δ, and ε, the proliferating nuclear antigen, replication factor C complexes and replication factor A.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: 178 proteins are immunoprecipitated with both CDPK4-3xHA and MCM5-3xHA including all components of the ORC and the MCM complex.
source: We found 103 proteins interacting with CDPK4-3xHA, CDPK4-2xmyc and MCM5-3xHA indicating that CDPK4 and MCM5 share an overlapping molecular environment (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CDPK4 represented one of the most abundant interactors of MCM5-3xHA.
source: Consistently, CDPK4 represented one of the most abundant interactors of MCM5-3xHA.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: CDPK4 is part of the MCM2-7/Cdt1 complex.
source: Altogether this suggests that CDPK4 is part of the MCM2-7/Cdt1 complex and may regulate the pre-replicative complex to initiate DNA replication.
evidence: This is an inference from co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: CDPK4 may regulate the pre-replicative complex to initiate DNA replication.
source: Altogether this suggests that CDPK4 is part of the MCM2-7/Cdt1 complex and may regulate the pre-replicative complex to initiate DNA replication.
evidence: This is speculation based on the interaction data and known functions.

claim: Cytoskeletal proteins predicted to be components of the microgamete axonemes were the most abundant and significantly enriched cellular components in CDPK4 immunoprecipitates 10 min after activation.
source: Cytoskeletal proteins predicted to be components of the microgamete axonemes (Talman et al., 2014) were the most abundant and significantly enriched cellular components (p-value=5.10−4).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and statistical analysis.

claim: Most cytoskeletal components were also enriched in non-activated gametocytes.
source: It is however important to note that most of this cellular component was also enriched in non-activated gametocytes and that cytoskeletal proteins are abundant in male gametocytes (Khan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and citation to previous work.

claim: Nuclear proteins involved in DNA replication were much less abundant in CDPK4 immunoprecipitates at 10 min compared to earlier time points.
source: Nuclear proteins involved in DNA replication were nevertheless much less abundant compared to earlier time points (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Traces of CDPK4 were found to be incorporated in exflagellated male gametes.
source: Traces of CDPK4 were also found to be incorporated in exflagellated male gametes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 parts 4 and 5 - [Talman et al., 2014]) in accordance with a role in the initiation of axoneme activity.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and citation to previous work.

claim: Six proteins showed up to 8-fold increase in abundance in CDPK4 immunoprecipitates upon gametocyte activation which was not observed when CDPK4 was inhibited.
source: For 215 out of the 221 proteins immunoprecipitated with CDPK4-3xHA under all conditions, no obvious differences were detected between the three conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 part 8). However six proteins showed up to 8-fold increase in abundance upon gametocytes activation which was not observed when CDPK4 was inhibited (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Among the six proteins showing increased abundance upon activation were ORC1, ORC2, and ORC5.
source: Among these proteins were ORC1, ORC2, and ORC5, while the three remaining proteins were not functionally annotated.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PBANKA_110290 likely corresponds to a homologue of Cdc6.
source: PBANKA_110290 contained an AAA ATPase domain and a HMM profile analysis indicated that its closest homologue in human and yeast was Cdc6.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and homology searches.

claim: PBANKA_134880 likely corresponds to a homologue of ORC4.
source: Similarly, the closest homologue of PBANKA_134880 was ORC4 in human and yeast.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and homology searches.

claim: PBANKA_051390 likely corresponds to a homologue of ORC3.
source: Finally, homologues of PBANKA_051390 were only found in Plasmodium and Babesia but encoded a PF07034 PFAM domain corresponding to the N-terminus of ORC3.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and domain identification.

claim: 30% of MCM5-3xHA was present in the high salt fraction in non-activated gametocytes.
source: Western blot analysis showed that 30% of MCM5-3xHA was present in the high salt fraction in non-activated gametocytes.
evidence: This is supported by fractionation and Western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The ratio of MCM5-3xHA in the high salt fraction almost doubled 15 s after activation.
source: This ratio almost doubled 15 s after activation but remained unchanged in the presence of 1294 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by fractionation and Western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The ratio of MCM5-3xHA in the high salt fraction remained unchanged in the presence of 1294.
source: This ratio almost doubled 15 s after activation but remained unchanged in the presence of 1294 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by fractionation and Western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Loading of the MCM2-7/Cdt1 complex onto ORC1-5/Cdc6 complex happens around 15 s after activation of gametogenesis and requires active CDPK4.
source: Altogether, this suggests that loading of the MCM2-7/Cdt1 complex onto ORC1-5/Cdc6 complex happens around 15 s after activation of gametogenesis and requires active CDPK4.
evidence: This is an inference from the co-immunoprecipitation and fractionation data.

claim: CDPK4 has been shown to be myristoylated in P. falciparum.
source: CDPK4 has previously been shown to be myristoylated in P. falciparum (Wright et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4G2A-2xmyc microgametocytes did not exflagellate.
source: As for CDPK4-KO parasites, CDPK4G2A-2xmyc microgametocytes did not exflagellate while a CDPK4-2xmyc control was not impaired (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: More than 85% of CDPK4G2A-2xmyc gametocytes remained haploid.
source: Consistently, more than 85% of CDPK4G2A-2xmyc and CDPK4-KO gametocytes remained haploid while 28% of CDPK4-2xmyc gametocytes became octoploid.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 65% of CDPK4G2A-2xmyc gametocytes showed spindle-like structures.
source: However 65% showed spindle-like structures showing that CDPK4 myristoylation is important to initiate the first round of DNA replication but nor for mitotic spindle assembly (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CDPK4 myristoylation is important to initiate the first round of DNA replication but not for mitotic spindle assembly.
source: However 65% showed spindle-like structures showing that CDPK4 myristoylation is important to initiate the first round of DNA replication but nor for mitotic spindle assembly (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data comparing G2A mutant phenotypes.

claim: CDPK4-2xmyc shows two bands on Western blots: one around 63 kDa and one around 55 kDa.
source: Western blots of CDPK4-2xmyc revealed a large band in non-activated gametocytes close to the expected size of 63.1 kDa and a second band migrating around 55 kDa (Figure 3B), a pattern that was conserved during gametogenesis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 part 2).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In CDPK4G2A-2xmyc extracts, the large isoform migrated slower.
source: In CDPK4G2A-2xmyc extracts, the large isoform migrated slower.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The large CDPK4 isoform is myristoylated.
source: In some instances myristoylation has been shown to accelerate electrophoretic mobility (Demetriadou et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2011) suggesting that the large isoform is myristoylated.
evidence: This is an inference from the altered migration pattern of the G2A mutant and citations to previous work.

claim: The 55 kDa CDPK4 band did not show a different mobility in the G2A mutant.
source: Conversely, the 55 kDa band did not show a different mobility.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No significant evidence of CDPK4 palmitoylation was detected using an acyl-RAC assay.
source: Using an acyl-RAC assay, we were however not able to detect significant evidence of CDPK4 palmitoylation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 part 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 part 3.

claim: CDPK4 shows a broad cellular distribution in microgametocytes at 0 and 15 s after activation.
source: Immunofluorescence assays on CDPK4-2xmyc and CDPK4-3xHA, revealed that CDPK4 showed a broad cellular distribution in microgametocytes at 0 and 15 s after activation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 part 4).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: No obvious difference in CDPK4G2A-2xmyc localisation was detected at 0 and 15 s after activation.
source: We were however not able to detect any obvious difference in CDPK4G2A-2xmyc localisation at both time points.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 part 4.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of CDPK4-2xmyc and CDPK4G2A-2xmyc did not reveal any significant changes in interacting partners.
source: Similarly, immunoprecipitation of CDPK4-2xmyc and CDPK4G2A-2xmyc did not reveal any significant changes in interacting partners under the tested conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 parts 5 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: The CDPK4-2xmyc 55 kDa isoform was fully solubilised during hypotonic lysis.
source: The CDPK4-2xmyc 55 kDa isoform was fully solubilised during hypotonic lysis while 90% of the CDPK4-2xmyc large isoform was solubilised during hypotonic lysis and fully released with a subsequent carbonate treatment (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by fractionation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 90% of the CDPK4-2xmyc large isoform was solubilised during hypotonic lysis and fully released with a subsequent carbonate treatment.
source: The CDPK4-2xmyc 55 kDa isoform was fully solubilised during hypotonic lysis while 90% of the CDPK4-2xmyc large isoform was solubilised during hypotonic lysis and fully released with a subsequent carbonate treatment (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by fractionation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The large isoform in CDPK4G2A-2xmyc lysates was fully solubilised during hypotonic lysis.
source: Interestingly, the large isoform in CDPK4G2A-2xmyc lysates was fully solubilised during hypotonic lysis.
evidence: This is supported by fractionation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A minor population of myristoylated CDPK4-2xmyc was found in the NaCl fraction which was not observed for CDPK4G2A-2xmyc.
source: We found a minor population of myristoylated CDPK4-2xmyc in the NaCl fraction which was not observed for CDPK4G2A-2xmyc.
evidence: This is supported by fractionation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A major population of CDPK4 is soluble whereas a minor population of the large CDPK4 isoform is associated with membranes and possibly with chromatin.
source: Altogether this highlights that a major population of CDPK4 is soluble whereas a minor population of the large CDPK4 isoform is associated with membranes and possibly with chromatin.
evidence: This is an inference from fractionation data.

claim: The short CDPK4 isoform corresponds to a shorter protein whose translation is initiated at methionine +57.
source: As the short CDPK4 isoform did not appear to be myristoylated, we hypothesised it may correspond to a shorter protein whose translation could be initiated at a second start codon. The only possible second start codon upstream the catalytic domain was methionine +57, which we replaced by a codon coding for an alanine residue (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 part 1). The resulting CDPK4M57A-2xmyc line only expressed the large isoform (Figure 3D) confirming that the translation of the 55 kDa isoform is initiated at a second start codon and cannot be myristoylated.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that M57A mutation eliminates the short isoform.

claim: Microgametocytes expressing only the large 63 kDa myristoylated isoform progress to the octoploid stage and assemble axonemes but show a dramatic reduction in exflagellation.
source: Phenotyping of this line revealed that microgametocytes only expressing the large 63 kDa myristoylated isoform, progressed to the octoploid stage, assembled axonemes but showed a dramatic reduction in exflagellation compared to a control line (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The large CDPK4 isoform is mainly required to initiate the first round of DNA replication.
source: Altogether this demonstrates that the large CDPK4 isoform is mainly required to initiate the first round of DNA replication while the short non-myristoylated isoform is essential to complete late gametogenesis (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data comparing different mutants.

claim: The short non-myristoylated CDPK4 isoform is essential to complete late gametogenesis.
source: Altogether this demonstrates that the large CDPK4 isoform is mainly required to initiate the first round of DNA replication while the short non-myristoylated isoform is essential to complete late gametogenesis (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data comparing different mutants.

claim: Either short or long CDPK4 isoforms seem to support mitotic spindle assembly.
source: Interestingly, either short or long CDPK4 isoforms seem to support mitotic spindle assembly.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data showing spindle formation in both G2A and M57A mutants.

claim: Nineteen peptides were found to be thiophosphorylated by AS-CDPK4S147G.
source: Nineteen phosphopeptides were found to be thiophosphorylated by AS-CDPK4S147G.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Seventy phosphopeptides on 61 proteins showed a 2-fold increase at 18 s post XA activation in the WT but not in the CDPK4-KO line.
source: Phosphoproteomic analysis revealed that 70 phosphopeptides on 61 proteins showed a 2-fold increase at 18 s post XA activation in the WT but not in the CDPK4-KO line.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomics data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: SOC1, SOC2 and SOC4 are phosphorylated by AS-CDPK4S147G and could represent early effectors of CDPK4.
source: Among these latter, SOC1, SOC2 and SOC4 are phosphorylated by AS-CDPK4S147G and could represent early effectors of CDPK4.
evidence: This is an inference from combining AS-kinase and phosphoproteomics data.

claim: GAP40 and SOC3 were not differentially phosphorylated in the CDPK4-KO line but were robustly identified as phosphorylated by AS-CDPK4S147G and could represent CDPK4 effectors to control late gametogenesis.
source: Conversely, GAP40 and SOC3 were not differentially phosphorylated in the CDPK4-KO line but were robustly identified as phosphorylated by AS-CDPK4S147G and could represent CDPK4 effector to control late gametogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference from combining AS-kinase and phosphoproteomics data.

claim: GAP40 could not be deleted in asexual stages, suggesting an essential role in erythrocytic asexual multiplication.
source: GAP40 could not be deleted in asexual stages, suggesting an essential role in erythrocytic asexual multiplication.
evidence: This is an inference from the inability to generate knockout parasites.

claim: Knocking-out SOC4, SOC5 or SOC6 did not produce any defect in exflagellation or DNA replication.
source: Knocking-out SOC4 or the SOC5 and SOC6 controls did not produce any defect in exflagellation nor DNA replication while SOC1, 2 and 3 KO lines showed a strong reduction in exflagellation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SOC1-KO, SOC2-KO and SOC3-KO lines showed a strong reduction in exflagellation.
source: Knocking-out SOC4 or the SOC5 and SOC6 controls did not produce any defect in exflagellation nor DNA replication while SOC1, 2 and 3 KO lines showed a strong reduction in exflagellation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SOC1-KO and SOC2-KO lines showed a defect in DNA replication.
source: For SOC1-KO and SOC2-KO lines a defect in DNA replication was observed while SOC3-KO was not impaired in DNA replication and axoneme assembly.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SOC3-KO was not impaired in DNA replication and axoneme assembly.
source: For SOC1-KO and SOC2-KO lines a defect in DNA replication was observed while SOC3-KO was not impaired in DNA replication and axoneme assembly.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SOC1-KO line showed a dramatic reduction in exflagellation and 50% of microgametocytes remained haploid.
source: SOC1-KO line showed a dramatic reduction in exflagellation and 50% of microgametocytes remained haploid (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SOC1 is likely a CDPK4 effector to control loading of the pre-replicative complex.
source: As SOC1 phosphorylation requires CDPK4 activity within the first 20 s it is likely that SOC1 is a CDPK4 effector to control loading of the pre-replicative complex.
evidence: This is an inference from the timing of phosphorylation and the phenotype of SOC1-KO.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation of SOC1-3xHA identified MCM proteins and CDPK4 as abundant interactors.
source: Consistently co-immunoprecipitation of SOC1-3xHA in non-activated gametocytes identified MCM proteins and CDPK4 as abundant interactors (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: SOC1-3xHA showed a diffuse cytoplasmic localisation.
source: As observed for CDPK4-3xHA and CDPK4-2xmyc, SOC1-3xHA did not show a significant enrichment in the nucleus but rather showed a diffuse cytoplasmic localisation (Figure 5B) raising the possibility it may also have other functions during male gametogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 40% of SOC1-KO microgametocytes reached the octoploid state.
source: Interestingly, 40% of SOC1-KO microgametocytes reached the octoploid state suggesting this protein is not essential to initiate the next two rounds of DNA replication.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SOC1 is not essential to initiate the next two rounds of DNA replication.
source: Interestingly, 40% of SOC1-KO microgametocytes reached the octoploid state suggesting this protein is not essential to initiate the next two rounds of DNA replication.
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data.

claim: Eukaryotic homologues of SOC1 contain SAPS domains that have been found to be involved in G1 to S-phase transitions by associating to SIT4 phosphatase.
source: Eukaryotic homologues contained SAPS domains that have been found to be involved in G1 to S-phase transitions by associating to SIT4 phosphatase (Luke et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: SOC1 is expressed in asexual blood stages.
source: SOC1 is also expressed in asexual blood stages and its deletion was associated with a slight fitness cost in these stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2) suggesting its role is conserved in multiple stages of the Plasmodium life cycle.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2.

claim: Deletion of SOC1 was associated with a slight fitness cost in asexual blood stages.
source: SOC1 is also expressed in asexual blood stages and its deletion was associated with a slight fitness cost in these stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2) suggesting its role is conserved in multiple stages of the Plasmodium life cycle.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2.

claim: SOC1's role is conserved in multiple stages of the Plasmodium life cycle.
source: SOC1 is also expressed in asexual blood stages and its deletion was associated with a slight fitness cost in these stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2) suggesting its role is conserved in multiple stages of the Plasmodium life cycle.
evidence: This is an inference from expression and fitness data.

claim: SOC2-KO line showed a dramatic reduction in exflagellation.
source: The SOC2-KO line showed a dramatic reduction in exflagellation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Proportions of haploid microgametocytes in SOC2-KO were similar to its WT counterpart.
source: Unlike SOC1-KO, proportions of haploid microgametocytes in 10 min activated microgametocytes were similar in the KO and its WT counterpart indicating that SOC2 is not required for initiation of DNA replication and DNA replication per se (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SOC2 is not required for initiation of DNA replication and DNA replication per se.
source: Unlike SOC1-KO, proportions of haploid microgametocytes in 10 min activated microgametocytes were similar in the KO and its WT counterpart indicating that SOC2 is not required for initiation of DNA replication and DNA replication per se (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental data.

claim: 47% of SOC2-KO parasites remained diploid and 20% and 16% reached the 4N and 8N levels, respectively.
source: However, 47% of the parasites remained diploid and 20% and 16% reached the 4N and 8N levels, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SOC2 represents a CDPK4 effector required to complete mitosis in order to enter the subsequent round of replication.
source: SOC2 could thus represent a CDPK4 effector required to complete mitosis in order to enter the subsequent round of replication.
evidence: This is an inference from the phenotype of SOC2-KO parasites.

claim: SOC2-KO rarely showed incorporation of α-tubulin into distinct mitotic spindles at 1 min post-activation.
source: As opposed to the 820cl1 parental line, we were rarely able to observe incorporation of α-tubulin into distinct mitotic spindles at 1 min post-activation, a phenotype similar to what was observed when control parasites were treated with 1294 prior to activation by XA (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SOC2-KO showed normal axonemes encircling the nucleus at 10 min post-activation.
source: At 10 min post-activation, SOC2-KO showed normal axonemes encircling the nucleus (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SOC2 is a 623 kDa protein that appeared to be specific to Plasmodium.
source: This 623 kDa protein appeared to be specific to Plasmodium (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 1) and is predicted to encode six transmembrane domains and six sialidase penultimate C-terminal domains.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and phylogenetic data.

claim: SOC2 is predicted to encode six transmembrane domains and six sialidase penultimate C-terminal domains.
source: This 623 kDa protein appeared to be specific to Plasmodium (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 1) and is predicted to encode six transmembrane domains and six sialidase penultimate C-terminal domains.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis.

claim: C-terminal 3xHA tagging of SOC2 only allowed detection of a c.a. 140 kDa protein.
source: C-terminal 3xHA tagging of SOC2 only allowed detection of a c.a. 140 kDa protein, 70% of which was extracted in PBS.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: 70% of the SOC2-3xHA detected protein was extracted in PBS.
source: C-terminal 3xHA tagging of SOC2 only allowed detection of a c.a. 140 kDa protein, 70% of which was extracted in PBS.
evidence: This is supported by fractionation data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The detected SOC2-3xHA protein contained the peptide phosphorylated by CDPK4.
source: Interestingly, this protein contained the peptide phosphorylated by CDPK4.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of SOC2-3xHA recovered peptides mapping on the last 1137 amino acids.
source: Immunoprecipitation of SOC2-3xHA recovered peptides mapping on the last 1137 amino acids suggesting SOC2 is processed into at least two different isoforms.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: SOC2 is processed into at least two different isoforms.
source: Immunoprecipitation of SOC2-3xHA recovered peptides mapping on the last 1137 amino acids suggesting SOC2 is processed into at least two different isoforms.
evidence: This is an inference from mass spectrometry data.

claim: The 3xHA tagged C-terminal end of SOC2-3xHA was found to colocalise with mitotic spindles.
source: The 3xHA tagged C-terminal end of SOC2-3xHA was found to colocalise with mitotic spindles further suggesting a role in their assembly (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: SOC2 is expressed in asexual blood stages.
source: Similarly to SOC1, SOC2 is also expressed in asexual blood stages and its deletion was associated with a strong fitness cost in these stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2) suggesting a conserved role in mitotic spindle assembly during the atypical schizogony of Plasmodium parasites.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2.

claim: Deletion of SOC2 was associated with a strong fitness cost in asexual blood stages.
source: Similarly to SOC1, SOC2 is also expressed in asexual blood stages and its deletion was associated with a strong fitness cost in these stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2) suggesting a conserved role in mitotic spindle assembly during the atypical schizogony of Plasmodium parasites.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2.

claim: SOC2 has a conserved role in mitotic spindle assembly during the atypical schizogony of Plasmodium parasites.
source: Similarly to SOC1, SOC2 is also expressed in asexual blood stages and its deletion was associated with a strong fitness cost in these stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2) suggesting a conserved role in mitotic spindle assembly during the atypical schizogony of Plasmodium parasites.
evidence: This is an inference from expression, fitness, and localization data.

claim: SOC3-KO clone did not exflagellate.
source: Finally, SOC3-KO clone did not exflagellate but defects neither in DNA replication nor in axoneme assembly could be detected (Figure 5E) suggesting it represents a crucial effector of CDPK4 to complete cytokinesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: SOC3-KO showed no defects in DNA replication or axoneme assembly.
source: Finally, SOC3-KO clone did not exflagellate but defects neither in DNA replication nor in axoneme assembly could be detected (Figure 5E) suggesting it represents a crucial effector of CDPK4 to complete cytokinesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: SOC3 represents a crucial effector of CDPK4 to complete cytokinesis.
source: Finally, SOC3-KO clone did not exflagellate but defects neither in DNA replication nor in axoneme assembly could be detected (Figure 5E) suggesting it represents a crucial effector of CDPK4 to complete cytokinesis.
evidence: This is an inference from the phenotype of SOC3-KO parasites.

claim: SOC3-3xHA was found to partially colocalise with axonemal α-tubulin in exflagellating microgametes.
source: Concordantly, SOC3-3xHA was found to partially colocalise with axonemal α-tubulin in exflagellating microgametes (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: SOC3 is mainly expressed in the male gametocyte.
source: As opposed to SOC1 and 2, SOC3 is mainly expressed in the male gametocyte (Otto et al., 2014) and deletion of its coding gene was not associated with any growth defect of asexual blood stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and experimental data.

claim: Deletion of SOC3 was not associated with any growth defect of asexual blood stages.
source: As opposed to SOC1 and 2, SOC3 is mainly expressed in the male gametocyte (Otto et al., 2014) and deletion of its coding gene was not associated with any growth defect of asexual blood stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 2.

claim: SOC3 is restricted to Plasmodium species.
source: Phylogenetic analysis indicated that SOC3 is restricted to Plasmodium species suggesting that the molecular function of SOC3 is highly specific to control the activation of male gametocyte axonemes.
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 part 1.

claim: The molecular function of SOC3 is highly specific to control the activation of male gametocyte axonemes.
source: Phylogenetic analysis indicated that SOC3 is restricted to Plasmodium species suggesting that the molecular function of SOC3 is highly specific to control the activation of male gametocyte axonemes.
evidence: This is an inference from phylogenetic distribution and functional data.

claim: Deletion of soc1 and soc2 did not block the 1N/2N and 2N/4N transition as drastically as CDPK4 inhibition.
source: Deletion of soc1 and soc2 did not block the 1N/2N and 2N/4N transition as drastically as CDPK4 inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing KO and inhibitor phenotypes.

claim: Other identified or non-identified CDPK4 substrates cooperate with SOC1 and SOC2 to load the pre-replicative complex and assemble mitotic spindles.
source: This strongly suggests that other identified or non-identified CDPK4 substrates cooperate with SOC1 and SOC2 to load the pre-replicative complex and assemble mitotic spindles.
evidence: This is an inference from the incomplete phenotype of SOC1 and SOC2 knockouts.

claim: Multiple kinases and phosphatases have been shown to control male gametogenesis.
source: In addition, multiple kinases and phosphatases have been shown to control male gametogenesis (Guttery et al., 2012; Tewari et al., 2010) and changes in phosphorylation levels between 0 and 18 s after activation highlighted a broad phospho-dependent response.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Changes in phosphorylation levels between 0 and 18 s after activation highlighted a broad phospho-dependent response.
source: In addition, multiple kinases and phosphatases have been shown to control male gametogenesis (Guttery et al., 2012; Tewari et al., 2010) and changes in phosphorylation levels between 0 and 18 s after activation highlighted a broad phospho-dependent response.
evidence: This is supported by phosphoproteomics data from this study.

claim: A plastic phosphorylation-dependent network underlies regulation of the initiation of DNA replication and mitotic spindle assembly.
source: It is thus likely that a plastic phosphorylation-dependent network underlies regulation of the initiation of DNA replication and mitotic spindle assembly and the exact molecular roles of SOC1 and SOC2 and of their phosphorylation remains to be elucidated.
evidence: This is speculation based on the complexity of the phosphoproteome and incomplete phenotypes.

claim: Deletion of soc3 completely blocked exflagellation.
source: Conversely, deletion of soc3 completely blocked exflagellation suggesting that SOC3 may be a focal component for the activation of axoneme motility.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: SOC3 may be a focal component for the activation of axoneme motility.
source: Conversely, deletion of soc3 completely blocked exflagellation suggesting that SOC3 may be a focal component for the activation of axoneme motility.
evidence: This is an inference from the complete block of exflagellation in SOC3-KO.

claim: CDPK4 activity is essential only during two short time windows: within 10 to 30 s after activation and seconds prior to exflagellation.
source: During microgametogenesis, CDPK4 activity is essential only during two short time windows: within 10 to 30 s after activation and seconds prior to exflagellation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing timing of 1294 effects.

claim: CDPK4 is likely integrating multiple signals to be active at the right time and place.
source: This highlights that CDPK4 is likely integrating multiple signals to be active at the right time and place.
evidence: This is an inference from the temporal specificity of CDPK4 requirement.

claim: During the first window, CDPK4 is activated by a PKG-dependent Ca2+ mobilisation that occurs ten seconds after XA stimulation.
source: During the first window, the kinase is activated by a PKG-dependent Ca2+ mobilisation that occurs ten seconds after XA stimulation (Brochet et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Myristoylation of the large CDPK4 isoform is required to initiate the first round of DNA replication but not to initiate axoneme motility.
source: Myristoylation of the large CDPK4 isoform is another signal required to initiate the first round of DNA replication but not to initiate axoneme motility.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data with G2A and M57A mutants.

claim: Both large myristoylated and short non-myristoylated isoforms seemed to support mitotic spindle assembly.
source: Interestingly, both large myristoylated and short non-myristoylated isoforms seemed to support mitotic spindle assembly.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing spindle formation in both G2A and M57A mutants.

claim: Myristoylation per se is not essential for CDPK4 activity in vivo in the absence of the 56 amino acids upstream of methionine +57.
source: This indicates that myristoylation per se is not essential for CDPK4 activity in vivo in the absence of the 56 amino acids upstream of methionine +57.
evidence: This is an inference from the M57A mutant phenotype.

claim: Full length non-myristoylated recombinant CDPK4 proved to be an active enzyme in vitro.
source: In vitro, full length non-myristoylated recombinant CDPK4 proved to be an active enzyme suggesting myristoylation is important for in vivo regulation (Ojo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Myristoylation is important for CDPK4 in vivo regulation.
source: In vitro, full length non-myristoylated recombinant CDPK4 proved to be an active enzyme suggesting myristoylation is important for in vivo regulation (Ojo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference from comparing in vitro and in vivo data.

claim: Global profiling of protein myristoylation in human revealed that a large part of N-myristoyltransferase substrates are localised to the nucleus and mediate nuclear processes.
source: Intriguingly, global profiling of protein myristoylation in human revealed that a large part of N-myristoyltransferase substrates are localised to the nucleus and mediate nuclear processes (Thinon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The additional 56 amino acids upstream the second start codon may represent a regulatory domain to control CDPK4 nuclear functions.
source: Collectively, this suggests that the additional 56 amino acids upstream the second start codon not only serves as an extra sequence to accommodate N-terminal myristoylation but may also represent a regulatory domain to control CDPK4 nuclear functions.
evidence: This is speculation based on the functional differences between isoforms and knowledge about myristoylated proteins.

claim: CDPK4 is regarded as a potential target for a transmission blocking strategy.
source: CDPK4 is regarded as a potential target for a transmission blocking strategy and proof of principle that chemical inhibition of CDPK4 by bumped kinases inhibitors such as 1294 can block Plasmodium transmission in vivo has been demonstrated (Ojo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Chemical inhibition of CDPK4 by bumped kinases inhibitors such as 1294 can block Plasmodium transmission in vivo.
source: CDPK4 is regarded as a potential target for a transmission blocking strategy and proof of principle that chemical inhibition of CDPK4 by bumped kinases inhibitors such as 1294 can block Plasmodium transmission in vivo has been demonstrated (Ojo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4 strict essentiality during malaria transmission is likely explained by its multiple functions.
source: It is likely that CDPK4 strict essentiality during malaria transmission is explained by its multiple functions identified in this study.
evidence: This is an inference from the multiple roles identified in the study.

claim: Bumped kinase inhibitors such as 1294 appear to have a broad-spectrum anti-protozoal activity by targeting functional orthologues of CDPK4.
source: Bumped kinase inhibitors such as 1294 appear to have a broad-spectrum anti-protozoal activity by targeting functional orthologues of CDPK4 (Van Voorhis et al., 2017) and this study provides a first insight into the molecular functions of this atypical Ca2+-dependent protein kinase.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4 has been previously reported to be important for sporozoite motility.
source: Remarkably, CDPK4 has been previously reported to be important for sporozoite motility (Govindasamy et al., 2016) and oocyst formation (Billker et al., 2004), two processes unrelated to male gametogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4 has been previously reported to be important for oocyst formation.
source: Remarkably, CDPK4 has been previously reported to be important for sporozoite motility (Govindasamy et al., 2016) and oocyst formation (Billker et al., 2004), two processes unrelated to male gametogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In Toxoplasma gondii, the functional orthologue of CDPK4 (TgCDPK1) is essential for host cell egress and invasion.
source: Similarly, in the related apicomplexan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, the functional orthologue of CDPK4 (TgCDPK1) is essential for host cell egress and invasion (Lourido et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CDPK4 likely represents a pleiotropic regulator of the cell cycle during gametogenesis and a broad spectrum regulator of multiple other biological processes in the Apicomplexa.
source: It thus likely that this kinase not only represents a pleiotropic regulator of the cell cycle during gametogenesis but also a broad spectrum regulator of multiple other biological processes in the Apicomplexa.
evidence: This is speculation based on the multiple roles identified in this study and previous reports in other stages and species.

claim: In non-activated parasites, around 85% of male gametocytes were haploid.
source: In non-activated parasites, around 85% of male gametocytes were haploid.
evidence: This is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 part 8.

claim: A majority of diploid parasites could be observed between 30 s and 1 min after XA activation.
source: A majority of diploid parasites could be observed between 30 s and 1 min after XA activation, while tetraploid microgametocytes were mainly detected between 2 and 5 min.
evidence: This is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 part 8.

claim: Tetraploid microgametocytes were mainly detected between 2 and 5 min after XA activation.
source: A majority of diploid parasites could be observed between 30 s and 1 min after XA activation, while tetraploid microgametocytes were mainly detected between 2 and 5 min.
evidence: This is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 part 8.

claim: The three rounds of genome replication seemed to be completed by 6 min when 75% of male parasites were octoploid.
source: The three rounds of genome replication seemed to be completed by 6 min when 75% of male parasites were octoploid (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 part 8).
evidence: This is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 part 8.
